llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (auto-updating OpenClaw) is plausible, but the runtime instructions ask the agent to read local config files, run high-privilege system commands, and call scripts that are not included — an incoherent and potentially risky combination.

dimensions.detail: The description (auto-updater for OpenClaw and skills) aligns with actions like checking versions, updating via npm, and restarting a gateway. However the SKILL.md expects a local PowerShell script (scripts/self-updater.ps1) and Windows-only APIs while the registry metadata provides no code, no install, and no OS restriction. Expecting absent script files and not declaring Windows as required is inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly direct the agent to read user files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json), parse schedules, call messaging APIs, run npm update -g openclaw and clawhub update --all, and restart the gateway. The skill declares no config paths or credentials, yet it instructs reading local config (which may contain tokens) and performing system-level changes — scope exceeds the declared surface and is potentially invasive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files, yet the docs show running a local script (scripts/self-updater.ps1) and require external tools (PowerShell, npm, clawhub). This mismatch (instructions expecting external scripts/tools but nothing provided by the skill) is incoherent and raises operational risk: the agent may attempt to run or fetch missing artifacts or rely on user-local scripts of unknown provenance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, but it will read local config files that likely contain API tokens for notification channels and may require elevated privileges for npm -g and restarting services. Required secrets are implicit (stored in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) rather than declared, which is a proportionality and transparency problem.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good) and autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default). Because the skill performs high-impact actions (updates, gateway restart, contacting external services), autonomous invocation increases blast radius — combine this with the other inconsistencies before enabling autonomous runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is instruction-only but tells the agent to run a local PowerShell script and to read ~/.openclaw/* config files (which may contain API tokens), perform global npm updates, and restart your gateway — yet no script or install is supplied and no OS is declared. That mismatch is risky. Before installing: (1) do not enable autonomous invocation on a system you care about; (2) ask the publisher for the missing scripts/source and an official homepage or repository; (3) inspect ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and cron files to see what tokens/config would be read; (4) prefer a skill that declares required credentials and includes code or a trustworthy install method; (5) test any updater in a sandbox or snapshot your system first. If you cannot verify the source and contents of the referenced scripts, do not install or enable this skill.
